record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is the class 2NPDA of languages accepted by two-way nondeterministic pushdown automata equal to the class 2DPDA accepted by two-way deterministic pushdown automata?

evidence.quote: A very important question--namely "is 2NPDA = 2DPDA ?"--is missing. We could not relate it to any of the open problems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A two-way pushdown automaton (2PDA) is a finite-state machine equipped with a read-only input tape whose head can move both left and right (with end-markers) and an auxiliary unbounded pushdown stack. A computation accepts when the machine enters a designated accepting state. The automaton is deterministic (2DPDA) if its transition function is single-valued, and nondeterministic (2NPDA) if multiple transitions are allowed from a given configuration. Let 2DPDA denote the class of languages accepted by two-way deterministic pushdown automata, and let 2NPDA denote the class of languages accepted by two-way nondeterministic pushdown automata.

Question: Does 2NPDA = 2DPDA? Equivalently, can every language recognized by some two-way nondeterministic pushdown automaton also be recognized by some two-way deterministic pushdown automaton?
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence (or separation) of 2NPDA and 2DPDA is a long-standing question dating back to work of Aho–Hopcroft–Ullman (1968) and Cook (1971). Subsequent literature, including a 2013 revisitation of two-way pushdown automaton simulations by Glück, discusses simulations and complexity (linear-time for 2DPDA, cubic-time for 2NPDA via Cook's theorem) but does not report a resolution of the language-class equality. No source found establishes 2NPDA = 2DPDA or a proper separation; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Simulation of Two-Way Pushdown Automata Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Linear-time simulation of 2DPDA and cubic-time recognition for 2NPDA, building on Cook (1971) and Aho–Hopcroft–Ullman (1968).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study simulations of 2DPDA/2NPDA without establishing language-class equality.
